title: Arakhin 20 - Heirs to a Promise

chapters.title: Comparing Erech Vows and Nedarim for Heirs
chapters.about: Stringencies of Erech vows over regular donation vows when the vower dies.

chapters.title: Vows Involving Limbs and Body Parts
chapters.about: Rules for vowing the value of a limb versus an essential part of the body.

chapters.title: A Baraita on Animal Vows and Affordability
chapters.about: Differences regarding animals, wild beasts, birds, and leniencies for poverty.

chapters.title: Rav's View on Partial Vows and Vessels
chapters.about: Analyzing whether vowing the Erech of a limb or vessel applies the market value.

chapters.title: Partial Payments and Gezerot
chapters.about: Discussions on paying half an Erech and the potential confusion between formulations.

chapters.title: Dedication of an Ox or House as a Korban
chapters.about: Responsibility when a specific dedicated item dies or is destroyed versus adding the word Deme.

chapters.title: Consecrating Something That Does Not Exist
chapters.about: Attributing the ruling that one can consecrate future property to Rabbi Meir.

summary: Rabbi Hidary goes through Masechet Arakhin, comparing the laws and stringencies of fixed Erech vows versus general market value vows. He analyzes how these vows apply to body parts, animals, and what obligations pass down to heirs when someone dies. The discussion also covers the opinions of Rabbi Meir and the Chachamim regarding whether a person can consecrate something that does not yet exist in the world.
questions: What happens to an Erech vow or a market value vow if the person who made it dies?
How does the law treat a vow made for a specific body part, such as an arm or a head?
Can a person consecrate something that does not yet exist in the world?
What is the difference between dedicating an animal itself and dedicating its monetary value?
